brief: Goldman's weekly equity positioning monitor (Robbie Stankard) reports four data sets without building a single argument. CTA Corner: trend-following models hold ~$43.5bn long global equities, down from $125bn a month ago and $67bn last week; baseline forecasts call for $3.5bn of selling over the coming week, with $5.5bn of US buying from SPX/NDX signals staying positive, and SPX pivot levels at 7704/7493/7012 (short/medium/long term). GS Prime Brokerage: global and US equities were net sold on the week, short sales outpacing long buys; overall net leverage fell to the 10th percentile and the L/S ratio to the 14th percentile over one year, even as some fundamental and US L/S leverage measures ticked up; hedge funds rotated into Industrials (fastest pace since January) and out of Health Care/Biotech, which is de-grossing at its steepest pace in five years. Buybacks: desks stayed sidelined in pre-earnings blackout but expect liquidity to inflect as earnings season starts, with ~10% back in open windows by week's end. Market breadth sits at its lowest since the Dot-Com Bubble.
